## About

I am a second-year MPH student in Epidemiology with a certificate in Applied Biostatistics and Public Health Data Science at Columbia University. I started this journey at McGill University, where I majored in Environment with a concentration in Ecological Determinants of Health in Society and minors in Statistics and Field Studies.

While at Columbia, I have really fallen in love with biostatistics. Partaking in research outside of my immediate interests has demonstrated that what I love is the story the numbers tell, no matter the subject matter. I want others to have this love as well, which led me to become a Teaching Assistant for Quantitative Methods of Public Health at Mailman. I loved how the courses I took for my statistics minor in undergrad challenged me, and have carried this knowledge into my applied biostatistics courses.

Recently, I have also embraced my interest in gastroenterological research by getting involved with GI research at Columbia, and I hope to continue pursuing this interest in my future career. I have also done research on antimicrobial resistance, often called the "silent pandemic," which I am now extending into my master's thesis.

I am graduating in May 2027 and am seeking biostatistics roles in pharma and biotech. You can find my [research](research.html), [projects](projects.html), [publications](publications.html), and [CV](cv.html) on this site, and a bit more about me outside of work [here](about.html).
